title: Sprint Echelon Allocation Protocol and Cross-Stream Staffing Playbook
creator: Nina Patel
description: Create an operational playbook for multi-stream sprint staffing that formalizes echeloned allocations (primary, secondary, float), surge triggers, and lightweight rotation rules. The goal is to reduce surprise mid-cycle hires, prevent single-person bottlenecks on cross-cutting initiatives, and provide a repeatable rubric for scope trimming tied to headcount and skill coverage.
goals: 1) Define 3-tier echelon model (Primary owners, Secondary coverage, Float pool) with headcount-to-scope mapping. 2) Provide decision rules for rebalancing mid-cycle when lead capacity changes by >20%. 3) Integrate playbook with cycle intake and cadence tooling so PMs can run allocation simulations during planning.
deliverables: 1) Playbook doc with decision matrix and sample allocations for typical initiatives. 2) Planning worksheet (CSV) and a simple allocation simulator (Google Sheet) for scenario modeling. 3) One-run trial with 3 initiatives in the next cycle and a retro report.
risks: 1) Overhead: introducing an allocation protocol can slow early-stage planning if too prescriptive. 2) Fairness perception: teams may view the float pool as penalizing ownership. 3) Tooling integration delays could force manual workarounds.
stakeholders: Product leadership (owner), Eng managers, Design leads, People Ops (headcount visibility), Solutions Eng for dedicated capacity customers
acceptance_criteria: Playbook published in Confluence with decision matrix and at least three example allocations
Allocation simulator accepts headcount and skill inputs and outputs recommended primary/secondary/float assignments
Trial completed with three cross-functional initiatives and a retro capturing at least two measurable improvements (reduced mid-cycle reassignments or faster TTR on blockers)
PMs and Eng managers sign off on the rubric in a walkthrough session
updates: 2026-02-21: Kickoff with Eng managers and two PMs. Aligned on need for explicit float pool and triggers for elevation. Agreed to keep float pool capped at 10% of active headcount for trial.
2026-02-27: Prototype allocation simulator created (Sheet link). Initial mapping: 6-week epic -> 3 primary engineers + 1 secondary + 1 float for high-complexity projects.
2026-03-03: Design feedback: want clearer ownership handoff notes for secondary owners. Added a short checklist for context transfer in the playbook.

2026-03-05: Eng review: suggested changing elevation trigger from 20% capacity delta to event-driven triggers (onboarding delays, unexpected bug spikes). Decision: keep both — percent-change for planning, event-driven for runtime adjustments.
2026-03-08: People Ops confirmed access to headcount forecast for next three cycles; will surface hiring freeze windows to avoid allocation conflicts.

2026-03-10: Draft published to Confluence for wider review. Requested signoffs scheduled for 2026-03-15 review session. Assigned follow-up to Marcus to run first trial allocations for initiatives A, B, and C. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/cycle-sim/pull/142
notes: Trade-offs discussed: conservative float pools reduce disruption but reduce throughput; larger float increases context switching. We will start conservative and measure throughput/incident rates. Will iterate thresholds after the trial cycle.
qa_plan: During the trial run, collect three metrics: number of mid-cycle reassignments, time-to-recover from critical blocker, and PM satisfaction (survey). Review results in post-cycle retro and iterate playbook rules.
implementation_steps: Finalize decision matrix and publish playbook
Operationalize allocation simulator and connect People Ops forecast feeds
Run one trial cycle allocations and monitor metrics
Collect retro feedback and update playbook rules and thresholds
